data.hook: McLane Stadium glowed yellow as Baylor fans cheered their Bears to a dominant bounce-back win, with backup QB Nate Bennett shining under the lights.
data.name: Baylor Bears Crush Prairie View A&M 44-3 in Home Opener
data.summary: After an early field goal by Prairie View A&M, Baylor surged ahead with 17 unanswered points in the first quarter and rolled to a 44-3 victory, amassing over 550 yards of offense. Nate Bennett went 23-of-35 for 301 yards, two touchdown passes including a 33-yard strike to Jayden McGowan, and a rushing score. The defense stifled the Panthers to 110 yards, while Rhett Armstrong kicked three field goals and fans in matching yellow shirts kept the energy high all night. Baylor evens its record at 1-1 ahead of Louisiana Tech next week.

data.hook: With just 14 seconds left and trailing by two, Brandon High Jr. burst 25 yards for the game-winner, sending UTSA fans into wild celebration on the road.
data.name: UTSA Roadrunners Rally Late to Claim 31-26 I-35 Rivalry Win
data.summary: The Roadrunners overcame a halftime deficit to beat Texas State 31-26 in San Marcos, securing their 100th program win and reclaiming the I-35 Showdown trophy with High's clutch touchdown run. Owen McCown passed for 214 yards and a score, while the defense forced key stops after Texas State led 17-7 at the break. Coach Jeff Traylor's squad improved to 2-0, now leading the series 6-2, as players kissed the hardware and posted 'TOOK BACK TEXAS.'

data.hook: Oklahoma's narrow loss to Michigan and Texas's last-second win over Ohio State on September 12 have traditional SEC fans venting online with memes and pleas to ship the newcomers back.
data.name: Fans Call for Texas and Oklahoma's Return to Big 12 After Early SEC Struggles
data.summary: Texas and Oklahoma joined the SEC ahead of the 2024 season for tougher competition and bigger payouts, but after Oklahoma fell 17-10 to Michigan and Texas scraped by Ohio State 24-23, frustrated supporters are flooding posts with calls to send them back to the Big 12. Fans point to past Big 12 blowouts and share memes like a dump truck plunging off a cliff or Norman Rockwell's 'Freedom of Speech' painting to argue the schools don't measure up. Some see it as typical rival banter mixed with real disappointment over inconsistent results.

data.hook: Fans checking scores Saturday night blinked twice at No. 22 Houston up 90-0 before halftime. It was a wild app glitch that had everyone double-checking reality.
data.name: Houston's 77-6 Rout Sparks App Glitch Confusion
data.summary: A glitch in the Real sports app showed absurd scores like 91-0 during Houston's game against Southern, prompting posts of shock and humor as users wondered if the Cougars were delivering an NBA-style beatdown. In reality, at TDECU Stadium, Houston dominated with a 77-6 win, scoring on their first 11 drives, racking up 388 rushing yards, and leading 49-0 at halftime despite a brief power outage. Southern managed just 121 yards total, and the teams shortened the fourth quarter to eight minutes; Houston moved to 2-0 while fans laughed off the mix-up with screenshots and quips like 'generational ass whooping.'
